newsitem.title: UK: Britain confirms it to elect MEPs by PR in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Britain confirms it to elect MEPs by PR in 1999.

text.p: Home Secretary Jack Straw on Thursday confirmed all Britain's 87 members of the European Parliament will for the first time be elected by proportional representation (PR) in 1999.
But he added this did not mean the government had become converted to the argument for PR to elect the British parliament.
"Time will be found for legislation this (UK parliamentary) session which will allow the next European Elections to be held using a system of PR," Straw said in a statement.
The moves means Britain will come into line with its 14 EU partners all of whom choose MEPs by a PR system.
Straw said the British mainland would be divided into regions each returning several MEPs, with seats being allocated to parties in each region in proportion to the votes cast for them there.
Previously there have been 84 British mainland single seats, and MEPs have been elected on a first-past-the-post basis.
In the 1994 elections, this resulted in Labour winning 62 seats, the Conservatives just 18 and the minority Liberal Democrats and Scottish Nationalists two each.

Straw said the three Northern Ireland MEPs will continue to be elected by the Single Transferable Vote system of PR, a system also used in the Irish Republic in which voters number candidates in order of preference.
He told journalists that the European Parliament was quite different from the British one in that it was not an executive body, but a representative one.
"So arguments about strong government, weak government do not arise," he said.
Defenders of the British first-past-the-post system argue that one of its main virtues is that it tends to produce a government with an overall majority in parliament, producing strong government.

However, Straw said a commission will be set up in the autumn to implement Labour's pledge to hold a referendum on whether to switch to a PR system for the British parliament. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
